reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust quasi-periodic pattern with an estimated fundamental period of ~92 points, confirmed across all candidates. Each cycle consists of a slow, roughly linear ascent (slope ≈ −0.005 to +0.001 per point in standardized units), followed by a sharper descent with occasional plateaus or minor inflections. Peaks are moderately sharp but not impulsive, typically reaching 1.8–2.2 standardized units; troughs are broader and shallower, often near −0.5 to −1.0, with occasional deeper excursions (down to −2.0) that recur consistently across cycles—suggesting structured low-frequency modulation rather than isolated anomalies. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is stable at ~2.1–2.4, and roughness/curvature metrics are nearly identical across candidates (0.1349), indicating highly repeatable local dynamics. Noise is low-level, jagged, and symmetric around the trend, with no evidence of heteroscedasticity. Baseline level drifts slightly between segments (median from −0.20 to +0.27), but this appears systematic and reproducible—not random contamination. All candidates show clean, non-truncated boundaries relative to their window cycles, supporting integrity of the extracted motifs. Acceptable variation includes: (i) small shifts in peak timing (±2–3 points), (ii) minor differences in plateau duration, and (iii) consistent presence of one deep trough per 3–5 cycles, which is part of the normal morphology.
